nmsis_compute_profile_after_sync.measurement_scope: Generated model C and copied adapter instrumented with rdtime; official NMSIS computation and production runtime unchanged. Profile table is dumped after the ordinary numerical output via QMP before quit.
nmsis_compute_profile_after_sync.inputs: Reused saved seeded representative activations, real first-layer weight, ORT and FP64 references. QK/AV start at dynamic input buffers and exclude upstream layout producers.
limitations: rdtime is QEMU virtual time, not CPU cycles; function intervals include JIT and host descheduling.
Per-hart intervals overlap. Their durations must not be summed as wall time; interval unions are computed within each batch and then summed across serial batches.
Dispatch time outside active provider intervals includes synchronization, instrumentation and scheduling effects, not pure scheduler CPU time.
Each table column has an independent median; subtracting these medians need not equal the median of a per-run difference.
Instrumented timings diagnose the bottleneck; they do not establish a 10% performance-selection gain. Uninstrumented adjacent comparisons are required for admission.
nmsis_compute_profile_after_sync.current_policy: Existing poll and measured configuration retained; no change inferred from this diagnostic alone.

limitations: Only three formal observations per case/variant, local QEMU, saved seeded activations and real first-layer weights; no full-model or hardware speed claim.
